Subject: Mutual action: financial gate and unit-econ sanity for close

Hi Asha / Max —

Great to be lining this up. Before we lock the MAP and hit procurement, we need a short financial gate focused on unit economics so your finance and procurement teams have the numbers they need to sign off. I attached an initial cost model template (velaris_map_cost_model.xlsx).

High-level asks (can you confirm by EOD next Tuesday?):
- Traffic baseline: representative daily active sessions and peak qps (simple CSV would be fine).
- Tokens per session: current estimate (avg & P90) and any seasonal multipliers.
- Acceptance criteria: max tokens/$ target or acceptable monthly spend band for pilot (we want a clear gating rule).
- Any mandatory caching constraints or data residency needs that affect caching strategy.

Redwood assumptions to validate (we'll fill these in and share back before demo):
- Baseline batching: 16-64 window depending on latency SLO (we can tune).
- KV/prefix caching: expected 15-35% token reduction for conversational flows with stable prefixes.
- Model variant: we'll model a float16 and an 8-bit quant variant for cost tradeoffs.

Next steps
- You share traffic & tokens; Karthik will run the batch/cache sims; Ben will provide expected tokens/$ ranges based on the two model configs.
- If the numbers hit your gate we move to procurement SOW and reserved capacity planning.

Thanks — aim is to keep this lean so we don't slow the MAP.

— Lauren Bishop
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Mutual action: financial gate and unit-econ sanity for close

Thanks Lauren — appreciate the template. Quick answers and a couple asks from our side:

- Traffic baseline: attached is last 30 days (daily_dau_peak.csv). Typical DAU ~18k, peak qps ~55.
- Tokens per session: avg ~420 tokens, P90 ~1,100 tokens (these include context).
- Procurement/gate: finance wants a pilot budget cap of $25k/mo but open to per-token SOW if expected spend is lower.
- Caching: we have PHI masking rules — caching of patient name fields is not permitted. We can cache templated prompts/prefixes but need auditability.

Open questions:
- How sensitive are your cost sims to P90 vs avg token counts? If we do a conservative P90-based sim can we still show a path to the $25k cap?
- Do you support a delegated prefix cache that excludes patient-identifying slots? That would preserve auditability.

I looped in procurement@velarishealth.com for timelines — we are targeting a pilot start week of Dec 14.

Cheers,
Asha
Head of Product, Velaris Health
asha@velarishealth.com

Thanks for the details, Asha — good context on the PHI constraints. A few notes on how we'll model this and the assumptions I need you to confirm: 

Assumptions I'll use for the sims 
- Workload split: 70% templated Q&A (good cache hit rate), 30% free-form clinical summarization (low cache).
- Conservative cache hit for templated flows: 25% token reduction overall (we'll run sensitivity for 15/25/35).
- Batching windows: 16 tokens/windows for low-latency (target p95 < 400ms) and 48 for latency-relaxed endpoints (p95 < 900ms).
- Model variants: base LlamaX-7B f16 and LlamaX-7B int8 (quantized).
- Throughput: we'll assume reserved Dedicated for pilot with burst headroom.

Questions for Velaris: 
- Can you confirm the % of requests that are templated prefixes versus free-form? That drives cache lift.
- Do you expect an increase in session length during peak hours? (affects P90 sensitivity)

Ben — can you drop the expected tokens/$ for these two variants (we'll model both) and attach the batching profile we use internally? I can run the sims and push numbers back into Lauren's spreadsheet.

-Karthik
Principal Inference Engineer, Redwood Inference

Quick numbers from perf/cost bench (pilot scale, reserved Dedicated pricing):
- LlamaX-7B f16: ~0.0048 USD/token (baseline, no cache).
- LlamaX-7B int8: ~0.0025 USD/token (quant tradeoff, small quality delta).
- With a 25% effective token reduction from prefix caching: tokens/$ improves ~33% (example math in attached).
- Batching profile (attached) shows average batch sizes of 28 for warm traffic, 12 for cold — we model both windows in the spreadsheet.

Attachment: redwood_batching_profile.pdf (pdf, 98KB)

If Velaris keeps P90 at 1,100 and traffic split is 70/30 templated, rough monthly spend:
- f16 variant: ~ $48k/mo
- int8 variant: ~ $25k/mo
With conservative 25% cache we estimate: f16 ~ $36k/mo; int8 ~ $18.5k/mo. This suggests int8 + caching meets the $25k pilot cap. We should run a P90-sensitivity sim (Karthik).

Happy to sync tomorrow for a five-minute readout.

— Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Asha / Max — thanks for the fast turnaround and for looping procurement. Quick summary & agreed acceptance criteria to put into the MAP so procurement has clear sign-off language: 

Agreed decisions (to include in MAP):
- Pilot model & cost target: LlamaX-7B int8 with prefix caching enabled; expected pilot spend <= $25,000/mo under the conservative P90 sim.
- Caching policy: prefix caching only (no PHI fields); Redwood will provide audit logs for any cached keys and an opt-out toggle.
- Batching defaults: low-latency endpoints use 16-window; background/async endpoints use 48-window. These are configurable post-launch.
- Acceptance checkpoint: finance will review actual billing after 30 days of pilot; if spend > $25k we will trigger a joint re-plan (MAP rollback to canary/scale-down).

Action items and owners (dates):
- Velaris: Share traffic split by Nov 30 (Asha).
- Redwood: Karthik to run P90 sensitivity sims and populate the spreadsheet by Dec 3.
- Redwood: Ben to attach final pilot SOW cost table and Reserved capacity estimate to HubSpot by Dec 6.
- Velaris procurement: review draft SOW and provide procurement comments by Dec 9.
- Both: Pilot start target Dec 14 (soft launch), 30-day billing checkpoint Jan 13.

Links: HubSpot deal — https://hubspot.example.com/deal/VH-2026-013; MAP folder — https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/velaris-map-docs

If this captures it please reply with an explicit sign-off phrase so procurement can treat this as the financial acceptance criterion (example: “Velaris confirms acceptance of int8 + caching pilot budget cap $25k/mo for Dec 14 start”).

Lauren Bishop

Redwood Inference
